fix(notifications): Space the sidebar notifications apart again

RSI's "#billing .content ul { margin: 0 }" took the space between a notification and the list below it, and above a list at the top of the box; both rules now carry the weight of an ID.

Refs #96

Keep refused comment runs in their container (carve#5806) Refs markup-carve/carve#5806 (carve-js) Refs markup-carve/carve#5818 (carve-js) This implements the ticket's **Expected (what the fix implements)** section. A shallow closer now stays with an item's open refused comment run. A description retains brace-shaped middle lines as paragraph text when a later shallow closer refuses the authored run. Item input: ```crv - {% a {k=v} z %} y ``` Before: ```html
  • {% a

z %} y

``` After: ```html
  • {% a {k=v} z %} y
``` Description input: ```crv :: t : {% a {k=v} z %} y ``` Before: ```html
t
{% a

z %} y

``` After: ```html
t
{% a {k=v}

z %} y

``` The review found a same-owner description boundary that the first lookahead crossed. This implements carve#5818's **Expected (what the fix implements)** section for carve-js. Boundary input: ```crv :: t : {% a {k=v} : next ``` Before: ```html
t
{% a
next
``` After: ```html
t
{% a {k=v}
next
``` The boundary check also makes that earlier `
` independent of a `%}` later in `: next`. The spec model still has the gap tracked by carve#5818. No corpus row changed. Focused parser tests, TypeScript, and touched-source lint passed on the current head. Generated item and description sweeps compared 1,440 brace-middle variants with the spec model at carve main: 1,440 agreed, 0 differed. A separate 2,000-case boundary sweep confirmed that the first description retains its refused run with and without a closer after the next description. Another 408 inner-marker and heading-shaped variants were added to the existing active tickets carve#5809 and carve-js#4856. Median HTML render timing on repeated affected shapes on the latest head, with concurrent CI load: 2,048 bytes 35.125 ms; 8,192 bytes 108.234 ms; 32,768 bytes 455.197 ms. No limit changed. codex review (medium): first pass found cross-description lookahead, fixed by 7d97e05c; second pass found that a later block opener containing `%}` was absorbed by an item, fixed by 5faccf61. The third pass found an interrupted quote paragraph with a stale comment-run tracker; ca498bc0 prevents the list item from claiming that later closer. The fourth pass found that a heading between the opener and later closer became paragraph text; 7267fb77 stops that lookahead at the heading. codex review (medium), final pass: "The changes address the refused comment-run cases without an identifiable regression. The new targeted tests pass."

benchmarks.task_description: Wrap the theme switch's choices when the browser's text is larger, rather than scroll them out of sight When the browser's text was set larger and the theme switch's column was narrower than its row, the switch scrolled sideways inside itself and "Dark" sat out of sight, behind a scroll bar the page hides. - `.dk-theme-switch` now wraps its choices onto as many rows as they need where they do not fit, with the same gap between rows as between choices. Only a word wider than the column on its own still scrolls. Where the row fits, nothing changes. - In a demo's strip, which keeps one row of room for switches on their way, the switch keeps one row and scrolls as before, so nothing below the strip moves as it comes. - A browser test opens the switch in a 280px column with the root text at twice its size and finds every choice inside the switch and no sideways scroll. It failed before the change. - Another holds the switch to one row at the usual text size, at phone to wide widths, and a third holds it to one row in a strip. - The reference says the choices wrap where the column is narrower. fix(personal-agent): connector 0.1.19 terminal reasons say what holds a message back (TS port, W6c)

## What

Since connector 0.1.19 a running turn never holds a phone's message back: Claude Code queues it. The worker's words for the connector's terminal reasons (`core/src/locales/connector-reasons.ts`) follow:

- `terminal_busy` now says someone was typing in the terminal (or had it scrolled back) for 10 minutes; it no longer blames a running turn.
- New words for the `turn_end` codes 0.1.19 sends that the worker did not know (they fell back to "a reason I do not know"):
  - `terminal_input_withdrawn`: the queued message was pulled back into the terminal's input box; says where it is and how to send it.
  - `terminal_state_unknown`: the terminal's Claude Code could not be confirmed to hold the conversation for 10 minutes.
  - `read_only_live_session`: a prompt refused on a session that only watches a terminal's conversation.

Texts are verbatim from the Python worker. Ported from the Python worker.

## Tests

`core/test/remote/connector-reasons.test.ts`: the three codes join the connector's closed set; new tests (expectations as in the Python tests):
- a terminal turn error of connector 0.1.19 has its own words (8 codes),
- terminal busy no longer blames a running turn,
- a withdrawn message says where it is and how to send it.

Reverse proof: with the source of the base, 7 of 19 tests in the file fail (the closed set, every code in words, the three new codes, busy, withdrawn).

Ledger: 3 lines in `ported-tests/w6.txt`. `npm run check` green locally; public tree and message scans clean.

fix: don't cache an empty service filter when Dialogporten fails

<!--- Fortell kort hva PR-en din inneholder i to-tre setninger maks. -->

This PR fixes false successes - the bff returned an empty list to the frontend when the request failed or timed out, the response contained errors, or there was no session token. The end user saw an empty service list that was falsely cached as a success, so they had to refresh the page to fetch the list again.

It also reduces the retries for the service filter from 3 to 1, so the user waits about 1 minute instead of 2 before the query fails.

Added 5 tests to cover the different cases. Tested manually as well.

- #4750
